messages:
alex: Hey team — customer (acct 9876) reports intermittent 504s from the Go SDK on prod and we saw duplicate billing for two requests that should have been idempotent. Using go-sdk v1.2.0. Logs show 504 then immediate retry -> 200. Can someone triage?

devon: Which retry policy are they using? SDK defaults or custom? Also need snippet of how they construct http.Client.

alex: They call redwood.New() with default opts, no custom http.Client. Our support app calls client.Request(ctx, ...). Repro logs: 
```
2026-02-14T18:22:03Z ERROR request failed status=504 route=/v1/generate retry=0
2026-02-14T18:22:03Z INFO retrying request route=/v1/generate retry=1
2026-02-14T18:22:04Z INFO request succeeded status=200 route=/v1/generate retry=1
```
Billing shows two charge events for same logical request id.

maria: Ouch. Can you paste minimal repro (small Go program) and confirm whether they set per-request contexts with timeouts? Also what token/auth method — short-lived token or API key?

alex: Token via API key. Minimal repro they gave: 
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
defer cancel()
client := redwood.New()
req := redwood.GenerateRequest{...}
_, err := client.Generate(ctx, req)
```
No explicit http.Client config — SDK uses http.DefaultClient internally. They also have SDK retries enabled (default policy).

samir: Likely combination of: (1) using http.DefaultClient (no Timeout) + relying on ctx cancellation, (2) default http.Transport settings leading to slow header reads or stuck conns, and (3) SDK retry loop that immediately retries on 504 even for non-idempotent endpoints -> duplicate billing. Context cancel doesn't always abort at TCP level if Transport/Dialer not configured for timeouts.

samir: Short checklist to try: 
- Ensure request is made with req = req.WithContext(ctx) (SDK should already do this but confirm).
- Set a per-client Timeout (http.Client.Timeout) or ResponseHeaderTimeout on Transport so hung servers don't block.
- Configure Transport: DialContext, ResponseHeaderTimeout, TLSHandshakeTimeout, MaxIdleConnsPerHost, IdleConnTimeout.
- Honor Retry-After and only retry idempotent methods OR require idempotency-key header for mutating endpoints.
- Add Idempotency-Key header in SDK for generate/charge endpoints or expose opt-out for retries when billing-sensitive.

samir: Example recommended client config: 
```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConns:        200,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100,
  IdleConnTimeout:     90 * time.Second,
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
  ResponseHeaderTimeout: 15 * time.Second,
  DialContext: (&net.Dialer{
    Timeout:   10 * time.Second,
    KeepAlive: 30 * time.Second,
  }).DialContext,
}
client := &http.Client{
  Transport: tr,
  Timeout:   30 * time.Second, // overall per-request deadline
}
// Always call: req = req.WithContext(ctx)
resp, err := client.Do(req)
```

devon: For the SDK fix: default to a conservative http.Client.Timeout (30s) and set ResponseHeaderTimeout on transport. Also stop auto-retrying non-idempotent routes unless Idempotency-Key is present. Respect Retry-After header and exponential backoff with jitter. Patch proposal: add a RetryPolicy that checks method + idempotency header and server Retry-After before trying.

devon: Also note token refresh race: if we refresh tokens inside retry loop and a stale token causes 401 then immediate retry could also double-send. Make sure token refresh happens before retry or fail fast and re-auth outside of the charged request.

alex: Great, thanks. I'll ask customer to test with the transport + client.Timeout changes and add an Idempotency-Key for their mutating calls. Will also try temporary disable retries in their app to confirm duplicate billing goes away.

maria: Please include the repro program and attach billing IDs — I'll open a billing investigation after we confirm repro.

support-bot: Incident created INC-2026-042: "go-sdk 504 + duplicate billing" — assigned to eng-oncall. :white_check_mark:
